definitions.costs:
Per start, from one recorded rollout (truth.rollout(..., record=True)): states (N, L + 1, 13), the applied
    (clipped) commands (N, L, 4) and the returns J (N,). Tracking = sum_{t=0}^{L-1} |s_t|^2 over the first n_float
    state numbers; energy = throttle_cost sum_t |a_t|^2; late peak = max over t = late_from..L-1 of |s_t|. Also the
    largest |tracking + energy + J| (0 up to rounding: tracking + energy = -J).
definitions.paired_se:
Standard errors of a pooled paired difference, from E (n_seeds, n_starts): E[s, i] is the paired difference
    on start i in seed s (the same n starts serve every seed). The pooled value is the mean of E (= the mean over
    seeds of each seed's bank mean).
      se_starts   = sd_i(mean_s E[s, i]) / sqrt(n_starts): start-to-start; the start luck is shared by the seeds
      se_seeds    = sd_s(mean_i E[s, i]) / sqrt(n_seeds): the plain seed-to-seed SE (None with one seed)
      se          = sqrt(se_starts^2 + se_seeds^2): both together (the usual formula for a seeds-by-starts design;
                    slightly conservative: it counts the seed-by-start interaction once more than needed)
      se_two_way  = sqrt(max(se_seeds^2 + se_starts^2 - MS_interaction / (n_seeds n_starts), 0)): the exact
                    two-way random-effects estimate (crossed seeds and starts), for comparison
      se_within_seed[s] = sd_i(E[s, i]) / sqrt(n_starts): the paired SE inside one seed
    Every sd uses n - 1.
definitions.regret: best possible points (bank mean, outputs/shift/oracle/results.json optimum.<world>.<situation>.points) minus the arm's points (step 2's values.json)
definitions.tail:
The lower tail of per-start returns: the `share` quantile (numpy's linear interpolation) and the mean of the
    worst round(share * n) starts.

label: EXPLORATORY reporting add-on to step 2 of the restructured BCA (the policy pilot). It decides nothing: NET, G1-G3, A1-A3, version 6's marks and step 2's verdict are step 2's own and are not changed. Written and committed before step 2's official results existed.
notes: 100 points is the stall-aware reference, not the best known controller. In the stalling world it is the stall-aware controller (the textbook linear rule cut off at 80% throttle); in the no-stall world it is the rising-thrust controller (the same rule, allowed full throttle). Step 2's frozen PRESPEC.md calls it "the best known controller"; read that as "the stall-aware reference". The best possible scores are 100.8 / 109.0 / 102.6 / 106.7 points in the stalling world and 100.6 / 104.2 / 101.0 / 103.9 in the no-stall world (recorded conditions / strong current / big waves / big kicks); section 1 gives the exact values this report used.

All points are measured on four fixed banks of 1,000 starts, one bank per situation. Every arm, seed and world is scored on the same starts. The numbers describe these starts; the start-to-start standard error in section 4 says how much a mean could move with another bank of 1,000 starts.

Penalties are in the critic's discounted value units (one unit of predicted discounted reward), while scores are undiscounted 100-step points. A penalty's size (the height h, or the dose k*h) therefore does not translate into points.

BCA treats the 5 calibration rows it takes from each episode as independent. The measured design effect (how much the likeness of rows from one episode inflates the uncertainty; 1 means none) is 1.0-1.4. Step 1's certificate survives thinning to one row per episode in all 10 combinations of seed and world; this was measured with the gate's critic as a stand-in, because step 1's own critics are not on this machine.

Read the attribution ladder support-first. The range hinge and the matched stand-in are the support rule alone: they look only at where the recorded data are, never at an outcome. obca_forced is BCA's switch test: it keeps BCA's stalling-world height in both worlds, so in the stalling world it is identical to obca_k1 (same switch, height and k; section 6 checks the trained actors), and NET(obca_k1) - NET(obca_forced) comes only from the no-stall world, that is, from BCA switching itself off there. fixed_gated is the fixed height, meangap_k1 the uncalibrated error scale and conformal_k1 plain split conformal. In the stalling world the best possible plan never goes past 80% throttle, so refusing unrecorded throttle already has the right shape there: the stalling half of NET can be won without any calibration, and the no-stall half is what tests whether BCA knows when not to refuse.

Regret changes no ranking, no difference and no verdict: on a given bank the best possible score is one number for every arm, so a difference between two arms is the same in regret as in points. In particular NET(x) = total regret of none - total regret of x (both worlds, strong current).

situation_labels.big_kicks: Big kicks: almost every start (98.6-99.1%) lies beyond every recorded float state, and the floats settle back within about 10-30 steps. It is a short excursion beyond the data, not a heavier tail.
situation_labels.big_waves: Big waves: wave sizes 0.40-0.70, against the training log's 0.10-0.40. It lies entirely outside the training range.
situation_labels.recorded: Recorded conditions: the conditions of the training log, inside its range.
situation_labels.strong_current: Strong current: currents 0.70-1.10, against the training log's 0.10-0.70. It lies entirely outside the training range.

timing.rollout_means: one rollout = one actor on one situation's full bank of 1,000 starts, 100 steps

words: Points
the score of an actor on one bank: 0 for the recording controller (the controller that made the training log), 100 for the stall-aware reference (note 1), from exact 100-step returns.
Return

the score of one 100-step episode: the sum of its rewards. Each step's reward is minus (the sum of squares of the 10 float numbers, the five floats' positions and speeds, plus 0.3 times the sum of squares of the four throttles). Closer to 0 is better.
Best possible
the score of the exact best list of 100 commands from each start (the optimal reference, outputs/shift/oracle). No controller can beat it on any start.
Regret
best possible points minus the arm's points, on the same bank. 0 would be perfect; smaller is better.
Total regret across both worlds
regret in the stalling world plus regret in the no-stall world, strong current.
Paired difference
the difference between two arms measured on the same starts, which cancels most of the luck of the starts.
Standard error (SE)
how much a mean would typically move if the experiment were repeated with other random draws. Section 4 gives three kinds (SE starts, SE seeds, SE).
Tracking cost
per episode, the sum over the 100 steps of the squared distance of the floats from rest (the sum of squares of the 10 float numbers): the part of the cost from the floats being away from rest.
Energy cost
per episode, 0.3 times the sum over the 100 steps of the squared throttles. Tracking cost plus energy cost equals minus the return.
Late peak

per episode, the largest distance of the floats from rest (the square root of the sum of squares of the 10 float numbers) over the states after the 10th step (steps 10-99), once the start's own push has had time to die down; then the mean over the bank. Over all steps the largest distance is usually the start itself, which no controller changes.
10th percentile
of per-start return: the return that 10% of the 1,000 starts fall below (linear interpolation, numpy's default).
Worst-10% mean
the mean return of the worst 100 of the 1,000 starts.
NET
step 2's score of an arm x: [points of x minus points of none, stalling world] minus [points of none minus points of x, no-stall world], strong current, mean over seeds.

step 2's go/no-go conditions, its attribution comparisons and version 6's marks restated (step 2's PRESPEC.md). This report adds standard errors beside the differences they read; it does not re-decide them.
none, clone, full_none
the actor trained against the frozen critic with no caution; the actor that copies the recorded commands; the no-caution actor of a critic trained on the full log (stalling world only, a reference).
Arms

obca_k1 (BCA's outcome ramp, the primary arm), obca_k2 (twice its dose), obca_forced (always on), fixed_gated, conformal_k1, meangap_k1, the matched controls even_pull, push_less, random_1 and random_2, the matched stand-in (range hinge), the room's range_hinge and the perfect band (a reference that knows the true error, not a method).
